hints.content:
###The strategy

$\text{Area of a triangle} = \dfrac{1}{2}\cdot \text{base} \cdot \text{height}$

Before we can apply the formula to find the area of $\triangle ABC$, we must find the base and height of the triangle using the Pythagorean theorem (or the distance formula).

* The base is the length $AB$.
* The height is the length $CD$ (the base and the height always meet at a right angle).

###Step 1: Find the length $AB$



[[☃ image 1]]

$\begin{align} 
AB^2&= {\redE{3}^2 +\redE{12}^2 }  &&\text{Pythagorean theorem} \\\\
AB&= \sqrt{\redE{3}^2 +\redE{12}^2 }  &&\text{Square root both sides}\\\\
&=\sqrt{153} \\\\
&=\sqrt{9\cdot17} \\\\
&=\tealE{3\sqrt{17}}
\end{align}$

options.alt: A coordinate plane. Triangle A B C has point A at negative six, four, point B at six, seven, and point C at four, negative two. There is a slanted dashed line connecting from point C to a point D on side A B at a ninety degree angle at two, six. There is a highlighted horizontal line of twelve units that connects point B to a vertical highlighted line of three units to point A.

hints.content:
###Step 2: Find the length $CD$



[[☃ image 1]]

$\begin{align} 
CD^2&= \redE{2}^2 +\redE{8}^2  &&\text{Pythagorean theorem} \\\\
CD&= \sqrt{\redE{2}^2 +\redE{8}^2 } &&\text{Square root both sides} \\\\
&=\sqrt{68} \\\\
&=\sqrt{4\cdot17} \\\\
&=\goldE{2\sqrt{17}}
\end{align}$

options.alt: A coordinate plane. Triangle A B C has point A at negative six, four, point B at six, seven, and point C at four, negative two. There is a slanted dashed line connecting from point C to a point D on side A B at a ninety degree angle at two, six. There is a highlighted horizontal line of two units that connects point C to a vertical highlighted line of eight units to point D.

hints.content:
###Step 3: Find the area of the triangle

Using the base and height of $\triangle ABC$, we can find the area:

$\begin{align} \text{Area of a triangle} &= \dfrac{1}{2}\cdot \text{base} \cdot \text{height}\\\\
&= \dfrac{1}{2}\cdot AB\cdot CD \\\\
&= \dfrac{1}{2}\cdot(\tealE{3\sqrt{17}})\cdot(\goldE{2\sqrt{17}}) \\\\
&= 3\cdot \sqrt{17}\cdot\sqrt{17} \\\\
&= 3 \cdot 17 \\\\
&= 51
\end{align}$

###The answer:

The area of $\triangle ABC$ is $51$ units$^2$.

[[☃ explanation 1]]

options.explanation:
Yes, we can find the area of the outer rectangle, then subtract the areas of the triangular regions outside of $\triangle ABC$.



[[☃ image 1]]

$\begin{align}
\text{Area}_{\triangle ABC} &= 12(9) - \text{Area}_{\triangle1} - \text{Area}_{\triangle2} - \text{Area}_{\triangle3} \\\\
&=108 - \dfrac{1}{2}(12)(3)-\dfrac{1}{2}(2)(9)-\dfrac{1}{2}(10)(6)\\\\
&=108-18-9-30\\\\
&=51
\end{align}$

The area of $\triangle ABC$ is $51$ units$^2$.
